text.p: German utilities Lahmeyer AG and Rheinelektra said in a mandatory statement on Wednesday that they had completed a merger into one company, which will be called Lahmeyer AG.

The two units of diversified utility RWE AG said in mandatory statements on Monday morning that trading in the two respective shares would cease on Monday next and the new company would be listed on the stock exchange on April 21.
Shareholders in the two companies agreed the merger in February. From the time of the listing, shareholders will have three months to exchange their shares for shares in the new company.
For every three 50 mark shares, Lahmeyer shareholders would receive 32 new five-mark shares in the new group and 49 pfennigs per share in cash.
Rheinelektra shareholders would receive 64 five-mark shares in the new group and 34 pfennigs per share for every 50 mark share.
Both companies are over 60 percent owned by Essen-based RWE AG, one of Germany's biggest utility companies.
